The higher-dimensional source has k at least two, while every inequality in the normalized proof also holds for real k at least one. Setting d=1 reproduces the interval ledger row.

The tightened cap is contained in the original cap. A supporting plane of the compact convex body cannot contain the weighted centroid because the inward margin is positive on a positive-volume open subset and the density is at least one. Projection levels are null, and every open interval between the extrema has a positive-volume slab, so the upper-tail transform pushes unit volume to uniform measure.

Interpolating two caps by Minkowski addition gives a subset of the intermediate cap. The volume root is concave by Brunn–Minkowski, including the nonempty compact cap at the maximal coordinate. Jensen is with respect to total weighted mass 1+k alpha. On each quantile subinterval, the difference from its leftmost filling has zero integral, and subtracting the cutoff yields a nonnegative product.

Recomputed the slack at (1,alpha) as (q−1)+k alpha(q−alpha^(1/d))>0. At s=0 the slack is negative. A small reduction of both coordinates when r>0 holds s−r fixed, while lowering s alone when r=0 preserves its lower bound for small moves. Thus every minimizer is an interior s with nonlinear equality.

On a simplex, superlevel sets of a vertex barycentric coordinate are homothetic copies with factor 1−X. Hence the volume root is affine, and inserting the prescribed bands makes Jensen and the moment bound equalities. Their combined mass is alpha and the cap charges exactly s+r. At alpha=0, r=0, and at alpha=1, r=s. Both solve s=q^(−d).

Concavity of the power q−1 bounds its increment at s>0 by (q−1)(alpha−r)s^(q−2). The derivative lower bound is positive and has divergent integral towards infinity since q−2>−1. This gives exactly one positive root and the stated minimal feasible s for each admissible r.

dependencies.mapping: Use only the weighted Brunn–Minkowski inequality stated under External sources. Both caps at thresholds in the closed projection interval are nonempty bounded measurable compact convex sets, and their weighted Minkowski sum is compact and contained in the intermediate cap.

overlap.comparison: The metronoid depth inclusion at full mass gives the alpha=0 ordinary centroid lower bound and, after multiplying by two, the alpha=1 lower bound. It does not optimize the one-copy charge at intermediate alpha.

The accepted weighted three-tail inequality uses the centroid of uniform volume and shifted tails on the same body. Here the added measure changes the tested centroid, and the objective charges ordinary volume plus one copy of the added mass in a single cap.

readability: The variable in the one-dimensional integral is a tail rank, independent of the threshold argument of U. The scalar feasible region serves as a relaxation whose equality points are realized, which suffices for the sharp minimum.
